domainWarnings.detail: murakamiLaw: steel-derived small-defect law, R = -1 threshold amplitude; applied to AM alloys as a transfer
Murakami's small-defect law was derived for steels; it is applied to Ti-6Al-4V as a transfer
The cited Ti-6Al-4V applications are EBM and forged specimens, not this LPBF state.
The supplied size is 250 micrometres. The cited radlof2020 EBM Ti-6Al-4V horizontal specimen study reports 75 to 200 micrometres. This is a size-domain extrapolation.

validity.uncertaintyStatement: Uncertainty is unknown and may be large. Calibrate to your machine for better accuracy.
validity.explanation: Uncalibrated estimate: about 280 MPa fully reversed stress amplitude for an internal defect with projected square-root area 250 micrometres and hardness 330 HV. This is a defect-conditioned Murakami screening estimate for an R = -1 threshold scenario. It is not a fatigue strength at a stated cycle count and not an infinite-life endurance limit. Assumed defect scenario. The cited Ti-6Al-4V applications are EBM and forged specimens, not this LPBF state. Uncertainty is unknown and may be large. Calibrate to your machine for better accuracy.

uncertainty.construction: Murakami sqrt(area) law at the supplied size and hardness; no interval.

cycleTarget.text: No fatigue strength is given at 1e+07 cycles. The unmodified Murakami law is a threshold scenario and is nonconservative at very high cycle counts; a cycle-specific estimate needs an applicable sourced life model.

ctDetectionThreshold.text: Add the CT detection threshold and its validation method to describe which defect sizes may be missed.
